$comment: THE HOUSEHOLD CONSTRAINT STORE (v6, trimmed in v7). This is the ACCOUNT's copy of
household policy — the source of truth. It pushes DOWN to the device on every
dispatch; the device owns world state (what is in the fridge, what has been spent)
and never sources policy.
One entry per FACT, not per kind, so each carries its own provenance and lifetime:
kind         which constraints.hard / soft key it resolves into
value        list | number | string | window object
enforcement  hard = the Safety filter blocks on it · soft = planning bias only
source       account (a person entered it) | derived (real-world data) | chat (captured)
scope        household | domain | goal
applies_to   domains this entry is picked for; ['*'] = every domain
display_to   OPTIONAL, v7 — domains this entry's CHIP is worth showing on. Display
only: it has no bearing on resolution or enforcement. Absent = show
everywhere.
label        how the entry reads on a card. Soft entries need one: preferences are
rendered one row per ENTRY, so an unlabelled preference reads as its kind.
expires_day_offset  retires itself this many days from today (omit = permanent)
RESOLUTION (memory/store.py — deterministic, no LLM):
- hard LIST kinds (allergens, dietary, medical) are UNIONED across every entry,
applies_to IGNORED. The enforced set is never narrowed by relevance: a wrong
relevance pick must cost a noisy plan, never a safety miss.
- hard SCALAR kinds (budget_cap, quiet_hours, peak_hours, away_window) ARE
domain-picked: most specific applies_to wins, ties go to the stricter value.
- soft entries are picked by relevance (LLM, with applies_to as the fallback).
v7 — WHAT WAS REMOVED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A REGRESSION.
There is no budget_cap, no budget_envelope and no quiet_hours entry in this
household any more. That is a deliberate emptying of the STORE, not a removal of
the mechanism: those kinds are still first-class in store.py, the device's
policy.json still carries the numeric_cap and time_window_block rule instances
that enforce them, and the device gates still exercise both against synthetic
policy blocks. Nothing resolves, so nothing is dispatched, so nothing is shown.
Put an entry back and the whole chain works again with no code change.
Dates are DAY OFFSETS resolved against today at load — the same generic-clock rule the
device data files follow. Absolute dates go stale between demos.
$comment_members: Who lives here. Matches the device's data/family.json roster (which holds the diets,
dislikes and ages used for menu grounding); this list is the account's copy.

$comment: The three enforced-always rules. applies_to stays ['*'] because that is what the
union ignores anyway; display_to is the v7 addition and is DISPLAY ONLY. A
home-prep goal still carries all three on its dispatch and the Safety filter still
blocks on them — no step of a home-prep plan can trip them, so the card does not
spend three chips saying so.

dinner cleanup beat (21:00 sits inside the peak window) for no safety reason.

$comment: The away window, derived from the trip in the shared calendar. Offsets match the
device's data/vacation.json (depart +1, return +8).
SCOPED TO vacation_prep, not ['*'], and that is a deliberate limit: the seeded world
has the family eating dinners at home on days 1-6 AND away on days 1-8, so a
household-wide away window would block the meal demo's appliance proposals. Widening
it to ['*'] — which is the more honest rule, and would catch a meal goal preheating
the oven mid-trip — requires the world data to agree on when the family is away first.
v7-M5 is exactly that work: an away window written on the approval of a home-away
goal, household-scoped, with dates the user actually said.
constraints.label: away window
constraints.note: trip in the shared family calendar

$comment: MEAL PREFERENCES — the two the v7 demo shows, and the only two tagged to meal_plan.
One entry per preference ROW: the confirmation card renders soft entries one row
each from their provenance, so bundling several ideas into one entry would collapse
them into a single unreadable line.
